text:
sophie: heads up — multiple customers escalated rerank 5xx/timeouts starting ~09:12 UTC. seeing gateway 502/504 and customers reporting elevated p95. any eyes?
ryan: looking now. graphs show rerank.p95 jump from ~90ms -> ~2.6s between 09:11:30-09:13:10. error pattern: upstream timeout + gateway 502s.
maya: alert triggered: rerank-route.p95 > 1500ms in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. paging oncall.
olga: quick note: we shipped a client change last night that removed client-side batching for rerank requests. i'm seeing single requests with candidates arrays >900 in traces.
samir: pasting some gateway log lines around 09:12 (redacted ids):
```
[09:12:02] req=zz1 route=/v1/rerank status=504 upstream_error="timeout" qps=450
[09:12:03] req=zz2 route=/v1/rerank status=502 retries=4 candidates=912 payload_size=2.2MB
[09:12:04] req=zz9 client=10.20.30.40 latency=2300ms downstream_status=504
```
ryan: trace for req=zz2 shows the gateway waiting on sorter fanout for ~1.8s; downstream returned slowly because kvcache miss rate spiked and backend recomputed scores. throughput briefly high but not enough to explain per-item latency.
olga: repro i did in staging to mimic the client change:
```
# generate 950 candidate ids and send single request
python tools/repro_rerank.py --count 950 --concurrency 3 --endpoint /v1/rerank
# observe sorting latencies and gateway 504s under concurrency
```
maya: created incident INC-2026-89, enabling full tracing and increasing logging for rerank. also raised circuit-breaker sensitivity for that route to reduce retry storm.
infra-bot: incident INC-2026-89 created by maya. collecting traces and attaching recent deployment diffs. :robot_face:
sophie: can we get kvcache hit/miss and key cardinality across the window? suspecting cache churn from sending non-canonical ids.
samir: kvcache: hit_rate fell from 72% -> 8% at 09:11:45. unique keys exploded (cardinality x6). looks like clients are sending raw ids that include session-specific prefixes.
ryan: that would cause mass recompute and backend load. mitigation suggestions: 1) enforce a max_candidates gate at gateway, 2) reject huge payloads >2MB with 413, 3) add a temporary canonicalization shim at the gateway for known partner clients.
olga: i'm implementing gateway rule to cap candidates to 300 for public API keys and return 413 with guidance header. for internal keys we will return 429 Retry-After to allow graceful backoff. starting rollout in ~8m.
maya: also deploying a deprioritization path: heavy requests routed to low-priority pool so control-plane and normal traffic keep low p95.
ryan: spinning up a stress job in qa: send 1k-candidate requests at 600 qps to validate cap and deprioritization. will post results.
sophie: support follow-up: tell affected customers to retry with smaller candidate lists, enable client-side batching, and watch token limits. prepare a canned response template.
olga: documenting reproducer and thresholds in confluence: /internal/ops/rerank-large-payloads. key thresholds: candidates >700 OR payload >1.8MB + concurrency >2 triggers miss storm.
samir: root-cause hypothesis: front-end change eliminated batching + included volatile id prefixes -> high key cardinality -> kvcache miss storm -> backend recompute -> long tail -> gateway circuit trips. RCA to be finalized after postmortem.
maya: monitoring shows p95 falling back to ~140ms ~12m after mitigations started. keeping incident open for one more hour for stability.
infra-bot: incident INC-2026-89 mitigated at 2026-03-18T09:30:45Z. postmortem scheduled.
sophie: nice triage. please add final RCA, customer comms draft, and short-term SDK patch plan here when available. :thumbsup:
